current.text: Minnesota traded away Julius Randle and Naz Reid and added LaMelo Ball. Ball, Edwards, Jaden McDaniels and Rudy Gobert are set as four of the five starters.
Coach Chris Finch said the team did Edwards a disservice by playing him on the ball so much.
With Ball on the team, Edwards is expected to play more off the ball. His catch-and-shoot volume should go up and his assists should go down.
His usage may go up, and he is expected to be more efficient with Ball taking some of the offensive load.
Ball and Edwards should both be able to keep their three-point volume.
Minnesota plays smaller now and has very thin big man depth. Its starting group may include three guards.
With the smaller lineups and Randle and Reid gone, his rebounds could rise to about 5 per game.
Minnesota plays 4, 2 and 4 games in our playoff weeks 19 to 21. The two-game week starts March 15, which is our semifinal week.
Minnesota has 13 back-to-backs, which is the league minimum.
The two-game semifinal week drops him to the bottom of his tier, behind Jayson Tatum, Giannis Antetokounmpo and Cade Cunningham. Picks 7 to 10 are reasonable. ESPN's rank of 5 is too high.
In auction terms, Josh sees him as a player worth 40 USD or more. He went for 45 USD in an auction mock.
If his free throws recover to 84 to 85%, he is probably about 11th overall.
Minnesota is expected to compete and win about 53 games, so it should not rest players to tank.

durable.text: He has never been a top 10 fantasy player in any format, even though he is drafted there.
He had a reputation for never missing time, with 79 games in each of the two seasons before last. He was hurt a lot last season and missed enough games to miss All-NBA eligibility.
He shoots threes at high volume, at around 40%. Two years ago he was the best catch-and-shoot shooter in the NBA.
His assist rate has fallen in each of the last three years. His turnovers have stayed fairly flat.
He was a good free throw shooter, around 84%, before last season's drop to under 80%.
Points and threes are his standout categories, both far above the top 250 pool. Turnovers are his clear weakness, even for a guard.
